requirements.requirement: Run a containerized web application on node1 as the unprivileged account appsvc
requirements.summary: appsvc (uid 1001) was created with subuid/subgid ranges for rootless podman (cmd-7debd2b4ba8849c9). The nginx:alpine container was pulled and run via `su -s /bin/sh appsvc` using rootless podman (cmd-186faa2fb6224fc3, cmd-a70ecb00528740db). Process listings repeatedly show conmon and nginx master processes owned by uid appsvc, both at initial run (cmd-2d9ed2666d4545fc) and after both reboots (cmd-b6943fe5389149be, cmd-838f09d6b69f4dd3).

The container was published with -p 8080:80. curl to both 127.0.0.1:8080 and NODE_IP:8080 returned http_code=200 at initial deployment (cmd-a70ecb00528740db), after the boot-start fix (cmd-b6943fe5389149be), and after the second reboot (cmd-838f09d6b69f4dd3). The after-executor global snapshot independently confirms a listening socket on 0.0.0.0:8080 via the rootless port-forwarder pasta (global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets), corroborating the rootless container's port binding.

requirements.requirement: Application starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: An OpenRC init script (/etc/init.d/appsvc-webapp) was created and added to the default runlevel (cmd-4075b685a48845c7), and manual rc-service start/stop/status control plus absence of a who login session for appsvc was verified (cmd-2d9ed2666d4545fc). A healthy pre-restart baseline was captured (boot_id 53c8268a..., HTTP 200, no login session; cmd-2922862fd0214b9f). Reboot 1 changed the boot identity to 0e7f2a28... but exposed a genuine boot-start bug (checkpath failure on freshly-created /run tmpfs; cmd-7df781ff49354cc1, cmd-ca653d7e6c8447cd), which was diagnosed and fixed by replacing checkpath with explicit mkdir/chown/chmod (cmd-2032751a77a64348, cmd-e2b771fa456c4215) and validated manually (cmd-b6943fe5389149be). A second, independent reboot then changed the boot identity again (0e7f2a28...->601c9539...) and the service auto-started via the OpenRC default runlevel with no manual intervention, serving HTTP 200 on both loopback and NODE_IP, with processes owned by appsvc and no login session present (cmd-1b33c5e0539241eb, cmd-ee14d9d08a6a4ae0, cmd-c497190d82514428, cmd-838f09d6b69f4dd3). The global after-executor boot-identity (601c9539-...) matches the second reboot's final state, corroborating the transition.

overall_summary: The task's three material outcomes (rootless containerized web app running as appsvc, served on port 8080, and boot-start persistence without a login session) are all satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. Notably, the restart-evidence trace does not merely show configuration: it captures a genuine pre-fix boot-start failure during the first reboot, the diagnosis and fix, and then a clean auto-start on a second independent reboot with a distinct boot identity, HTTP 200 confirmed on loopback and NODE_IP, correct process ownership, and no active login session for appsvc — satisfying the higher evidentiary bar required for boot/restart-related outcomes. Hygiene is generally good; the only issues are a bounded, fully-reverted troubleshooting mutation and some leftover diagnostic log files in /tmp.
limitations: The captured evidence relies on shell command outputs and does not include independent artifact verification (e.g., contents of the final /etc/init.d/appsvc-webapp file after the fix, beyond what was echoed during the heredoc write and syntax check).
ps output truncates the full conmon command line in several captures, but ownership (appsvc) and the presence of the nginx master process remain clearly legible.

No loginctl/systemd session manager exists on this Alpine node (busybox who/last used instead), a slightly weaker session-absence check than loginctl but standard for this OS and applied consistently across all checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to task prerequisites (package install, cgroups service, appsvc user/subuid/subgid creation, container run, OpenRC script authorship) or to bounded final-evidence collection (two reboots, which also satisfy the boot-persistence requirement). One troubleshooting experiment, cmd-87d6026b9f564329, directly stopped the container as appsvc bypassing the rc-service state machine to probe recovery behavior; this left appsvc-webapp in a stale 'already started' state that required an explicit rc-service zap correction in cmd-43b92472ddfb42a6 before the service could be restarted normally. This was a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted mutation with no lasting residue, so it is noted but weighted lightly. Executor-caused residue does remain in /tmp (apkupdate.log, install.log, podman-info-appsvc.log, reboot.log, reboot2.log, w.out), confirmed present in the after-executor global snapshot's temporary-files observation and absent from before-prepare; these are minor abandoned diagnostic log files, not security- or availability-impacting, but were never cleaned up.
